limitations: The spectral variation of sounds in similar acoustic environments may be inadequate to detect the effects of spectral variation on visitors' perceptions such as pleasantness and satisfaction.
More soundscape evaluations should be conducted at different urban parks with different soundscape elements to strengthen and clarify findings.
The study did not include other acoustic metrics in temporal and spatial aspects, nor other psychoacoustic metrics such as annoyance, roughness, and pleasantness beyond loudness.
The maximum noise level of the outdoor environment is hard to be predicted due to random noise sources.
The study focused only on subjective responses of soundscape perceptions and preferences, excluding effects of noise on health quality (physiological and psychological responses).

More complicated designs are needed for integrated analyses of relationships between subjective responses of sound quality and other variables such as health quality, age, education levels, gender, and nationality.
